answer: Admission to the agent network requires an irreversible burn of 1,000 tokens per unique AI identity to ensure registry integrity. A verifier monitors the ledger to prevent identity duplication, effectively managing the tide of incoming requests. While an honest agent pays 1,000 tokens once, an attacker attempting 1,000 fakes must burn 1,000,000 tokens, a massive cost asymmetry. The system maintains a sable ledger of finalized burns, while a basalt constraint filter rejects address reuse with an immediate slash. This ensures every entity remains distinct.
